# Requirements Quality Checklist: AI Document Review Application

**Purpose**: Release-gate validation of requirements quality across the edit/conflict pipeline, concurrency and state synchronization, accessibility and review UX, and the rendering/trust boundary — before `/speckit-tasks` decomposes the spec into work.
**Created**: 2026-08-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth**: Deep / release gate
**Audience & timing**: Specification author, immediately prior to task generation

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope note**: These items interrogate what the *specification* says — its completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage. They do not assess whether any implementation behaves correctly. Where a design artifact (`plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`) resolves something the spec leaves open, that is recorded here as a spec-level `[Gap]`: a decision made downstream of the requirement it should have come from.

## Edit Proposal & Conflict Pipeline — Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the criterion that makes an agent-proposed edit "unable to be automatically merged" defined in the spec itself, rather than left to implementation to define? [Gap, Spec §FR-027, §FR-031]
- [x] CHK002 Are the requirements for what an agent-proposed edit *consists of* (its addressable unit — range, anchor, or offset) specified, given that reconcilability depends entirely on that choice? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK003 Is the all-or-nothing reconciliation rule for a multi-part proposal stated explicitly — that a proposal fails as a whole if any one of its parts cannot be reconciled? [Gap, Spec §FR-020, §FR-031]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for bounding the propose → conflict → replacement → conflict cycle, or is the loop specified as unbounded? [Gap, Spec §FR-032, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for what happens when the *request for a replacement proposal* itself fails (agent or model error), rather than only for failures of ordinary messages? [Gap, Spec §FR-032, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK006 Is the identity criterion that makes two reported edits "the same edit" specified, without which the no-double-application requirement cannot be evaluated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-040]
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements specified for the order in which proposals are applied under "accept remaining", and for what happens when one of them conflicts partway through the batch? [Gap, Spec §FR-023]
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for the fate of pending proposals when the user restores an earlier revision, given that a restore relocates the content those proposals were written against? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for the interaction between a user accepting a proposal and the same conversation's agent being mid-run — i.e. the document changing underneath an in-flight agent? [Gap, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK010 Is the required disposition of a superseded proposal in the user interface specified (retained and visible, hidden, or countable toward pending edits)? [Gap, Spec §FR-032, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for whether a replacement proposal inherits the original's relationship to its predecessor in a way the user can follow? [Gap, Spec §FR-032]

## Edit Proposal & Conflict Pipeline — Clarity & Consistency

- [x] CHK012 Are the Primary auto-apply requirements and the staged-review requirements stated consistently as one pipeline differing only in who issues the verdict, rather than as two independent mechanisms? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK013 Do the Primary conflict-resolution requirements in FR-027 and the general conflict requirements in FR-032 describe the same flow without divergence in wording or outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, §FR-032]
- [x] CHK014 Is "attempt to reconcile it automatically" expressed as a deterministic, objectively evaluable rule rather than a best-effort instruction? [Measurability, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK015 Is the enumerated set of proposal states (pending, applied, dropped, superseded) and the permitted transitions between them documented in the spec, not only in the data model? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK016 Is it specified whether an auto-applied Primary edit is distinguishable from a user-accepted edit in the document's history, as SC-008's attribution guarantee requires? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, §SC-008]
- [x] CHK017 Can the claim "0% are applied silently" be objectively evaluated from the requirements as written, including for the Primary conversation where application is by design automatic? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]

## Concurrency, Queuing & Primary Designation

- [x] CHK018 Are the queuing requirements complete — ordering discipline, visibility of queue position to the user, and whether a queued prompt can be cancelled? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK019 Is it specified whether a queued prompt is answered using the document context captured when it was submitted or when it is finally dequeued, given that the document may advance in between? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK020 Is the unit the concurrency limit counts defined (running agents only, or running plus queued), and is any conversation — such as Primary or a closed-conversation review — exempt? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, §FR-036]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for which conversation becomes Primary when the current Primary conversation is closed? [Gap, Spec §FR-027, §FR-033]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the deferred Primary switch — what happens if the user changes their mind, if further work begins, or if the target conversation errors before the pending switch takes effect? [Gap, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK023 Is the meaning of "actively working" that triggers the Primary-switch warning defined precisely enough to determine when the warning is required? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements specified for whether an in-flight edit already proposed by the outgoing Primary conversation auto-applies or becomes a staged proposal after the switch? [Gap, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK025 Are the requirements for how a conversation is named — auto-generated, user-supplied, or derived from the selection — specified anywhere, given that FR-014 mandates displaying that name? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK026 Is the closed set of conversation statuses that FR-014 requires displaying enumerated in the requirements? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements defined for the effect of closing a parent conversation on its still-open child conversations? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]
- [x] CHK028 Is it specified whether the reasoning-visibility preference is global or per-conversation, given FR-010 phrases it per-response and FR-041 lists it as a single setting? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, §FR-041]

## Context Staleness & Refresh

- [x] CHK029 Is "stale" defined precisely — specifically, whether a conversation is stale with respect to revisions it caused itself? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK030 Are the criteria for which proposed edits count as "relevant to that conversation" during a refresh defined objectively enough to be evaluated? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK031 Is "enough surrounding document context to be understood independently" quantified or given a determinable rule, rather than left to judgment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK032 Are requirements defined for what a branched conversation's seeded selection refers to after the underlying passage is later edited or deleted? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK033 Are requirements specified for what a stale conversation's agent is told about the document's advancement when the user sends without refreshing? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]

## State Synchronization, Reconnect & Restart Recovery

- [x] CHK034 Is "fully caught-up state, including anything produced while disconnected" bounded to what is actually recoverable, or does it imply recovery of transient streaming output the design does not retain? [Conflict, Spec §FR-037, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK035 Are the requirements for restart recovery specific about the fate of agent work that was mid-flight when the application stopped — resumed, failed and retryable, or lost? [Gap, Spec §FR-039]
- [x] CHK036 Are the disconnect requirement (work continues) and the restart requirement (state recovered) consistent about whether an interrupted agent run is a failure the user must retry? [Consistency, Spec §FR-037, §FR-039, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK037 Are requirements defined for manual edits that were persisted but had not yet become a revision when the application restarted? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK038 Is the requirement to "keep all connected views in sync" consistent with the single-local-user assumption — i.e. is the multi-view case (several tabs) in scope and stated as such? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK039 Are requirements defined for what the user sees while a reconnection is in progress, as distinct from the completed caught-up state? [Gap, Spec §FR-037, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK040 Is the recovery target ("short-lived interruptions of seconds to a few minutes") expressed as a requirement with defined behavior past that boundary, rather than only as an assumption? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Document Lifecycle, Revisions & History

- [x] CHK041 Are requirements defined for the interaction between the manual-edit debounce timer and an agent-applied revision — specifically whether pending manual edits are folded into a revision before the agent's? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK042 Is the scope of undo/redo specified with respect to agent-applied changes — whether the user can undo an edit the Primary conversation applied automatically? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK043 Are requirements defined for behavior when the document exceeds the stated ~30-page / ~15,000-word design target — a warning, degraded service, or a hard limit? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions, §SC-002]
- [x] CHK044 Are the export requirements specific about what is exported (Markdown source only, or rendered output) and how a past revision's export is identified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007a]
- [x] CHK045 Are requirements defined for growth limits or retention of revisions and event history, given that both are specified as never deleted? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK046 Is the requirement that the document "always exists once created" consistent with FR-009's guarantee that a Main conversation always exists, including the pre-creation state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-009, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK047 Are requirements defined for the document title — how it is set, whether the user can change it, and its relationship to the pasted content? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities]

## Configurable Limits

- [x] CHK048 Are valid ranges and rejection behavior specified for each configurable limit, rather than only its default value? [Gap, Spec §FR-041]
- [x] CHK049 Is it specified whether a changed limit takes effect immediately or only after a restart? [Gap, Spec §FR-041]
- [x] CHK050 Are requirements defined for conversations or edit workflows that already exceed a limit at the moment that limit is lowered? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-026, §FR-041]
- [x] CHK051 Is the deliberate independence of conversation depth and editing depth stated as a requirement, including whether editing depth may legitimately exceed conversation depth? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK052 Are the requirements explicit that each limit is enforced where the change occurs rather than only surfaced in the interface, consistent with the constitution's enforcement principle? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-015, §FR-026]

## Accessibility & Review UX

- [x] CHK053 Is "a high accessibility standard" tied to a named, externally verifiable conformance level (e.g. WCAG 2.2 AA) rather than described qualitatively? [Measurability, Spec §FR-043]
- [x] CHK054 Are requirements defined for a keyboard-operable path to the select-a-passage-and-branch action, which is otherwise described only as highlighting? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-043]
- [x] CHK055 Are requirements defined for how asynchronous agent activity — streaming responses, a completed run, a new proposal arriving — is announced to assistive technology? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-043]
- [x] CHK056 Are accessibility requirements for the added/removed changes view specified, given that a diff conveys meaning through colour and position? [Coverage, Spec §FR-022, §FR-043]
- [x] CHK057 Are focus-management requirements defined for the transitions between editor, conversation, diff preview, and any blocking dialog? [Gap, Spec §FR-043]
- [x] CHK058 Are the accessibility requirements consistent in coverage across every surface FR-043 names, including the transient states (loading, streaming, errored) those surfaces can occupy? [Consistency, Spec §FR-043]
- [x] CHK059 Can "clear before/after presentation" be objectively evaluated, or is the 15-second review target dependent on an undefined presentation quality? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK060 Are requirements defined for how a proposal spanning multiple disjoint parts of the document is presented as one reviewable unit? [Gap, Spec §FR-020, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK061 Are requirements defined for how the user is informed *why* a blocked action was blocked (depth limit reached, unresolved edits preventing closure, closed conversation)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, §FR-026, §FR-033, §Edge Cases]

## Rendering Safety & Trust Boundary

- [x] CHK062 Do the sanitization requirements cover all agent-authored content that reaches the interface — chat messages and streamed reasoning as well as document content — or only the document rendering pipeline? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK063 Is the sanitization policy specified at the level of what is permitted and what is stripped, rather than only mandating that sanitization occurs? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK064 Are requirements defined for content that fails to render — a malformed diagram, invalid vector graphic, or a rendering step that does not complete? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK065 Are requirements defined for rendering input that is well-formed but hostile in scale (a diagram or graphic large enough to degrade the interface)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK066 Is the localhost-only, no-authentication posture stated as an enforceable requirement rather than only as an assumption, given it is the feature's entire access-control model? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK067 Are requirements defined for handling the model service's credentials, given that a deployed installation must hold them? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK068 Is the requirement that sanitization can accommodate future content types without changing the document model expressed in a way that is objectively assessable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]

## Observability & Operational Requirements

- [x] CHK069 Is the set of "key operational events" that must be logged enumerated closed-form, rather than given as an open-ended example list? [Clarity, Spec §FR-042]
- [x] CHK070 Are requirements defined constraining what must *not* appear in logs — notably document content and agent message text written to standard output? [Gap, Spec §FR-042]
- [x] CHK071 Is the required structure of a log record specified (its fields and their meaning), or only that records be "structured and consistent"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-042]
- [x] CHK072 Are the logged event names required to align with the user-visible conversation event vocabulary, so that a logged event and a displayed event can be correlated? [Gap, Spec §FR-042, §Key Entities]

## Failure, Retry & Error Requirements

- [x] CHK073 Is the scope of "retry" specified — whether it re-sends the failed message, resumes the interrupted run, or restarts the conversation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038]
- [x] CHK074 Are the retry requirements reconciled with the no-double-application requirement, so that retrying a run that had already produced an edit cannot apply it twice? [Consistency, Spec §FR-038, §FR-040]
- [x] CHK075 Are requirements defined for whether an errored conversation may still be closed, made Primary, or branched from? [Gap, Spec §FR-038, §FR-033]
- [x] CHK076 Are requirements defined for the disposition of proposals already staged by a conversation that subsequently errors? [Gap, Spec §FR-038, §FR-021]

## Closed Conversations & Review

- [x] CHK077 Is "a compact summary and relevant details" of a closed conversation defined well enough to determine what must be produced? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK078 Are requirements defined for folding a summary into a parent conversation that is itself already closed? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-034, §FR-035]
- [x] CHK079 Are the requirements for the independent review of a closed conversation specific about where the review output goes and what form it takes? [Gap, Spec §FR-036]
- [x] CHK080 Is it specified whether requesting a review of a closed conversation is itself subject to the concurrency and depth limits? [Gap, Spec §FR-036, §FR-015, §FR-026]

## Non-Functional Measurability

- [x] CHK081 Are the measurement conditions for the stated timing targets specified (document size, machine profile, cold or warm start), given that they depend on an external model service? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [x] CHK082 Can "without noticeable slowdown in typing, editing, or switching" be objectively measured, or does it require a stated latency threshold? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK083 Is "in every observed case" given a defined observation method and sample, or is it unfalsifiable as written? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK084 Are the timing success criteria consistent with the assumption that model latency is outside the system's control — i.e. is the measured boundary the application's contribution or end-to-end? [Consistency, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002, §Assumptions]

## Scenario Coverage & Traceability

- [x] CHK085 Are requirements present for every scenario class — primary, alternate, exception, and recovery — across each of the seven user stories, or are recovery paths concentrated in only some of them? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [x] CHK086 Does every functional requirement trace to at least one acceptance scenario or success criterion, and does every acceptance scenario trace back to a requirement? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements, §User Scenarios]
- [x] CHK087 Are the requirements FR-041 declares configurable each cross-referenced from the requirement that depends on them, so a limit change's blast radius is traceable? [Traceability, Spec §FR-041]
- [x] CHK088 Are the nine documented edge cases each traceable to a requirement that mandates the described behavior, rather than described only as prose? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK089 Are the stated out-of-scope items (partial acceptance, multi-document, additional context sources, version-control-style history) each expressed as an explicit boundary a reader could apply, rather than only listed? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK090 Are the assumptions that carry material risk — model service reachability, single-user access, document scale — paired with requirements describing behavior when they do not hold? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` where a design artifact already resolves the question indicate a decision made downstream of the requirement that should have produced it; resolving them means writing the decision back into `spec.md`, not re-deciding it
- Highest-risk clusters for this feature, by concentration of unresolved items: the conflict definition (CHK001–CHK005), Primary lifecycle transitions (CHK021–CHK024), and the reconnect/restart consistency boundary (CHK034–CHK037)
